issues.body:
Two compounding problems in the new "Verify native capabilities are compiled into the release binary" step:

A. Fail-open by construction. `if grep -aEq "..." "$binary"; then ... exit 1; fi` — when `$binary` does not exist, grep exits 2 and prints to stderr, but the command is an `if` condition so `set -euo pipefail` does not abort, the branch is not taken, and the step reports SUCCESS. Any path drift, rename, or profile/target change silently disables the gate with no visible signal.

B. The path is probably already wrong. `cargo tauri build` (unlike the plain `cargo build` used by gui.yml:690 whose output the e2e lanes read at gui/src-tauri/target/debug/sparq-gui, gui.yml:719/838) renames the compiled binary to Tauri's main-binary name, which defaults to `productName`. tauri.conf.json:3 sets `"productName": "sparq"` and no `mainBinaryName` override exists, and this workflow's own comment (release.yml:453-454) confirms Tauri derives artifact names from productName (`sparq_0.1.0_amd64.deb`). So the produced binary is most likely `target/release/sparq` (`sparq.exe` on Windows), and `target/release/sparq-gui` no longer exists after the rename.

Combined effect: the step that is supposed to prove the stubs are gone very likely greps nothing and always passes. Because release.yml is tag-triggered only, this is never exercised on a PR — the exact blind spot that let the original stub-shipping bug through, now masked by a green check. The rebuild-hint wording itself is fine: all four stubs (engine.rs:347, federation.rs:66-67, odrl.rs:221, forms.rs:89) do contain "rebuild the desktop app with" after Rust's line-continuation whitespace stripping.
issues.fix_hint:
Make the check fail closed and resolve the binary rather than guessing:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
ext=""; [[ "${{ runner.os }}" == "Windows" ]] && ext=".exe"
binary=""
for cand in "target/release/sparq${ext}" "target/release/sparq-gui${ext}"; do
  [[ -f "$cand" ]] && { binary="$cand"; break; }
done
if [[ -z "$binary" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: no release binary found under target/release" >&2
  ls -la target/release >&2 || true
  exit 1
fi
echo "checking $binary"
if grep -aEq 'rebuild (the )?desktop app with' "$binary"; then
  echo "ERROR: release binary contains a native-capability rebuild stub" >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

Stronger still, assert the POSITIVE as well (a string unique to each enabled path) so a future build that drops all four commands cannot pass by containing neither stub nor capability. Add a comment naming the four stub sites (engine.rs, federation.rs, odrl.rs, forms.rs) so the shared wording is not silently reworded out from under the grep.
issues.title: Capability check is fail-open: grep on a missing binary exits 2 inside `if`, so the step passes; the path is likely wrong anyway

issues.body:
The two new lanes are added to the `tauri-build` job, which is declared `continue-on-error: true` (gui.yml:458) and whose rows are named "GUI build + clippy (<label>, advisory)" — the job header (gui.yml:442-446) states the `advisory` keyword makes `ci-summary / gate` exclude the whole leg. So an `hdt`-gated or feature-unification compile error produces an advisory red that blocks nothing and merges anyway.

That is still an improvement over round 1 (the failure becomes visible pre-tag instead of at tag time), but release.yml's amended comment now asserts more than the evidence supports: "Linux rows ... the exact native release feature union is proven green by clippy in gui.yml" is the stated justification for keeping those rows BLOCKING (`soft: false`, release.yml:305-306). Two gaps in that claim: the lane is non-gating (it may be red at the moment the tag is cut), and `cargo clippy` runs the dev profile while the release build uses `[profile.release]` with `lto = true`, `codegen-units = 1` (gui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml) — clippy does not exercise that link surface.

Given the repo's honesty discipline about PROVEN vs DOCUMENTED-UNTESTED, this comment should not upgrade an advisory dev-profile clippy lane to "proven green".
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) split the two Linux rows of `tauri-build` into a gating job (no `continue-on-error`, no `advisory` in the name) so the union lane genuinely blocks — macOS/Windows can stay advisory — or (b) leave it advisory and downgrade the release.yml wording to what is true, e.g. "the release feature union is compiled by an ADVISORY (non-gating) clippy lane in gui.yml on the Linux rows; the release-profile build (lto=true, codegen-units=1) and the .deb/.AppImage bundle step are the new surface." Option (a) is what makes the `soft: false` Linux rows defensible.
issues.title: New hdt/union lanes sit in the advisory, continue-on-error, gate-excluded `tauri-build` job — they cannot block, yet release.yml now cites them as proof

issues.body:
The PR adds `cargo test --features hdt` alongside the existing `cargo test --features federation` and `cargo test --features odrl`, but adds no `cargo test --features forms`, even though `forms` is now shipped in the release bundle. The union lane is `cargo clippy --all-targets`, which COMPILES the tests but never executes them.

The forms-ON tests are the only executable evidence that the native bridge matches the direct `sparq_forms::derive_form` serialization — forms.rs:136 `applicable_shape_edit_and_view_match_direct_serialization` and forms.rs:166 `explicit_shape_request_matches_direct_serialization`, both `#[cfg(feature = "forms")]`. In the default lane only forms.rs:191 `lean_build_returns_actionable_unavailable_error` (the stub test) runs. So the behaviour of the capability this PR newly ships to end users is asserted by no executed test in any CI lane.
issues.fix_hint:
Add, mirroring the sibling lanes:

```yaml
      - name: Clippy (forms, -D warnings)
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets --features forms -- -D warnings

      - name: Test (SHACL-derived forms, native lane)
        run: cargo test --features forms
```

Optionally also run the union as a test rather than clippy-only (`cargo test --features hdt,federation,odrl,forms`) so every feature-ON test executes in the exact shipped combination.
issues.title: `forms` is the only newly-shipped feature with no `cargo test --features` lane — its feature-gated tests never run

verdict.summary:
Round 1's clearest defect is genuinely fixed: `forms` is now in the release feature list (gui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml declares it; forms.rs:80-93 is the stub it avoids), and gui.yml gained an `hdt` clippy+test lane plus a `hdt,federation,odrl,forms,custom-protocol` union lane. Direction is right and the feature list matches what cargo-tauri actually enables (tauri adds `custom-protocol` itself). But BOTH new safeguards are fail-open, so the defect class the PR exists to prevent can still ship green.

(1) The new "Verify native capabilities" step cannot fail for a missing file. `grep -aEq ... "$binary"` on a nonexistent path exits 2; because it is the `if` condition, `set -e` does not fire and the step PASSES. And the path is probably wrong: `cargo tauri build` renames the cargo binary to the Tauri main-binary name, which defaults to `productName` — `sparq` (tauri.conf.json:3), not `sparq-gui` (the workflow's own comment at release.yml:453 notes Tauri names artifacts from productName, e.g. `sparq_0.1.0_amd64.deb`; the `target/debug/sparq-gui` paths in gui.yml:719/838 come from plain `cargo build`, which does not rename). release.yml is tag-only, so a silently vacuous guard would never be noticed on a PR — the same blind spot as the original bug, now wearing a green check.

(2) The new lanes land inside gui.yml's `tauri-build` job, which is `continue-on-error: true` and whose row names carry `advisory` so `ci-summary / gate` excludes the leg (gui.yml:440-458). They cannot block a merge. release.yml's amended comment now claims the Linux rows' "exact native release feature union is proven green by clippy in gui.yml" and keeps those rows BLOCKING (soft:false) on that basis — an overstatement for a non-gating, debug-profile clippy lane.

Also: `forms` is the only shipped optional feature with no `cargo test --features` lane, so its feature-gated tests (forms.rs:136,166) never execute.
